newsitem.title: PERU: Lima shrs close with largest gain of year on GDP. [CORRECTED 19:45 GMT]
newsitem.headline: Lima shrs close with largest gain of year on GDP. [CORRECTED 19:45 GMT]

text.p: Shares on the Lima stock exchange ended Monday with the largest gain of 1997 as players believed forthcoming economic growth figures would be the best of the year and lead to solid company profits, brokers said.
The trend was seen continuing Tuesday, they added.

Monday, the General Index saw its highest daily rise this year, climbing 4.01 percent to 2,213.8 points. The blue-chip Selective Index also gained strongly, rising 3.02 percent to 3,198.6 points, according to preliminary figures given at the market's close.
"The bolsa is progressing very well and will continue firm so long as the expectation for the April GDP (gross domestic product figure) figure lasts," Manuel Torres of local brokerage Finvest said.
Local analysts have predicted April's year-on-year (GDP) figure -- set to be published this week -- will show the highest monthly rise of the year.

At the market's opening Monday, Santander Investment said April's year-on-year growth was likely to be as high as 13.7 percent. The government said Monday revised figures for 1996 showed a 1.8 percent year-on-year growth in April last year.
Benchmark Telefonica del Peru led the market up as it gained 4.11 percent to break for the first time the seven sol barrier, closing at 7.10 soles on volume of 1.7 million shares.
Polymetal miner Milpo gained most in the mining sector's ongoing bull run, climbing 10.0 percent to 42.96 soles on volume of 70,000.
Peru's largest brewery group Union de Cervecerias Perunas Backus y Johnston SA rose 6.15 percent to 2.76 soles on volume of 2.3 million shares.
